requirement_results.command: list_authorized returns only resources whose classification is dominated by the caller's clearance, verified against a real Fuseki dataset with UNCLASSIFIED/SECRET/TOP_SECRET resources
count_authorized always equals len(list_authorized) at every clearance level, by construction (structurally prevents the count-leak negative acceptance criterion)

a real, raw, marking-blind SPARQL COUNT over the same dataset differs from the authorized count for a low-clearance caller, demonstrating why marking-aware filtering is required and that the adapter's public API never exposes the raw number
exists_authorized returns the identical shape (a plain bool False) for a forbidden resource and for a resource that never existed, defeating an error-shape existence-probe leak

a resource ingested without its classification triple is never returned by list_authorized, even at the highest clearance -- the SPARQL marking join is fail-closed, not an implicit least-restrictive default
the serialized payload returned to a low-clearance caller never contains an unauthorized resource's identifier, label or classification anywhere in it
full local pytest regression, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)

residual_risks: The marking scheme used here (a 3-level totally-ordered classification lattice) is a minimal instantiation of ocor_runtime.c4_marking's general finite-lattice engine, chosen for spike clarity; the sealed engine itself supports arbitrary partial-order lattices and multiple concurrent schemes, neither of which this spike needed to exercise to prove the projection-safety property.

count_authorized and exists_authorized are deliberately implemented by deriving from list_authorized's own filtered result rather than independent SPARQL COUNT/ASK queries; this is what structurally guarantees they cannot diverge, but it means a production implementation optimizing for large result sets would need a different (still marking-safe) strategy, which is out of this read-side spike's scope.

This task added a real, ephemeral Fuseki service (via a build+run step, since infra/fuseki/Dockerfile is built from source rather than a pre-built pullable image) to the same 3 CI workflows already carrying a TypeDB service from OCOR-DEV-0017; every future PR now also builds this image in those 3 jobs.
The same pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test begins from adapter.reset() (a real SPARQL DELETE WHERE against the live in-memory dataset) so a fresh run from a clean or partially-populated dataset converges to the same state -- verified directly by 5 consecutive full test-suite runs with no manual cleanup between them. The CI provisioning step itself was rehearsed end-to-end locally (build, run, health-wait, query, teardown) on an alternate port before being added to any workflow.
